assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, the incretin effect, the active truncated peptide) led to incretin therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefit. The link from basic hormone physiology to a major medicine is clear and original, and the impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and therapeutic rationale of GLP-1 over decades; Mojsov's role in identifying the biologically active truncated GLP-1 is a recognised but contested part of the story. Knudsen's contribution is mainly industrial drug development. The three-person configuration is plausible but credit among the peptide-identification contributors is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent clinical confirmation across multiple drug classes, with robust outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is disputed.
Whether to recognise drug development (Knudsen) alongside physiology is a policy question and the supplied credited names alone do not resolve it.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new modality of cellular immunotherapy, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and now extending into myeloma and autoimmunity. The concept, the costimulatory design and the clinical proof are all clearly original and consequential.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design of costimulated second-generation CARs and the first successful clinical translation. Rosenberg's work on adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials is important, but the CAR-specific decisive contributions are best assigned to the first two. Early CAR concept work (Eshhar and others) is not in the supplied names and may complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of independent clinical follow-up. Long-term safety (secondary malignancy, durability) and solid-tumour limits remain active questions, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Contribution of the original chimeric-receptor concept by people not in the credited names.
Rosenberg's relative claim in a three-person configuration.
Long-term safety and durability in a wider population.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics, from microbial channelrhodopsins to cell-type-specific control in neurons, has become a basic tool across neuroscience, enabling causal tests of circuit function. Its originality and breadth of use are exceptional, although its impact is on research method more than on clinical medicine.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenböck made an earlier genetically targeted light-control proposal. Six names cannot fit a prize, and the choice between discovery of the actuator and its neuronal application is a real allocation problem. I propose a configuration weighted toward the discovery and demonstration.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for 15 or more years and in routine use. Clinical translation (vision restoration) is early, which does not detract from its value as a tool.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among the six credited people is unresolved.
Whether a tool discovery fits the physiology or medicine remit as well as a therapeutic one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of TOR and mTOR as the central controller of growth in response to nutrients and growth factors is a major conceptual advance. It links cell biology to cancer, diabetes, ageing and immunosuppression, and rapalogs have clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and showed its role in growth control. Sabatini and colleagues defined mTOR complexes and nutrient sensing in mammals. Schreiber's contribution on rapamycin and FKBP12 chemistry is significant but more tool and mechanism focused, so I would not include him in a limited configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed over three decades; clinical translation is real but narrower than the biological reach. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether to credit the rapamycin chemical biology (Schreiber) or the mammalian pathway work (Sabatini) alongside Hall.
Some of the later nutrient-sensing details are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer and are reducing cervical cancer incidence in vaccinated populations. This is a clear, original and highly consequential preventive-medicine advance. Note that zur Hausen's HPV-cancer discovery was already recognised in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer led a parallel VLP development and the Gardasil lineage. Other contributors (such as Jian Zhou, deceased) are not in the credited names, so the three-person configuration depends on how the committee reads that history.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data now show large reductions in infection and cervical neoplasia, with early evidence of reductions in invasive cancer. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the VLP technology and the role of deceased contributors.
Final cancer-endpoint evidence is still accruing in some cohorts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, and that its blockade works in patients, established the cytokine-targeted therapy concept and transformed treatment of several inflammatory diseases. It is a classic bench-to-bedside advance.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the concept and the clinical proof of principle with anti-TNF antibodies; the attribution to two people is clean and well documented.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; decades of use and biosimilars. Recognition could be viewed as late, which is not an obstacle.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views antibody engineering and TNF biology contributors outside the credited names as needing recognition.
Prior recognition (Lasker) is not a barrier but is not evidence of merit either.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of intracellular signalling, from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, and is relevant to secretory-cell disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is conceptually clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori identified the Ire1 and Hac1/XBP1 pathway and its mechanism. This is a clean two-person attribution, with possible additional claims from Kozutsumi, Ron and others that are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed across species. Clinical translation is still mostly indirect.
uncertainties: Contribution of other pioneers in ER stress signalling who are not credited.
Limited direct therapeutic impact so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 and its family define the core control of apoptosis, with the translocation-driven oncogene discovery leading to venetoclax and BH3-mimetic therapy. It is a strong link from basic cell death biology to cancer treatment.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the Bcl-2 family work; Vaux showed the survival (rather than proliferation) function in lymphoma models. Strasser's contributions are significant, and Tsujimoto's discovery of BCL2 in the t(14;18) translocation is not among the supplied names. This leaves allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with approved targeted drugs. Overlap with previously recognised apoptosis work (2002) needs careful consideration.
uncertainties: Originality relative to the 2002 prize on programmed cell death.
Credit among Cory, Adams, Vaux and Strasser, and Tsujimoto's absence.
Verified details of the historical priority are from my recollection only.
